relations.myth: Huwawa appeals to Utu after Gilgamesh’s betrayal
relations.note: Huwawa appeals to Utu for justice and his life.
Enlil appoints Humbaba guardian of the divine forest.
relations.source: Old Babylonian and Standard Babylonian Gilgamesh

relations.myth: Huwawa’s severed head is brought before Enlil
relations.note: Enlil rebukes Huwawa’s killers and redistributes his seven radiances.

relations.myth: Shamash’s winds immobilize Humbaba during the forest battle
relations.note: Shamash aids Humbaba’s attackers with winds that pin him down.

relations.myth: Humbaba appeals to Shamash but receives no rescue
relations.note: Humbaba weeps or appeals before Shamash, who does not save him.

relations.myth: Gilgamesh promises marriages to obtain Huwawa’s radiances
relations.note: Gilgamesh fraudulently offers sisters and gifts until Huwawa surrenders his protection.
Gilgamesh confronts, strikes, and captures Huwawa after removing his defenses.

relations.myth: Gilgamesh and Enkidu behead the pleading guardian
relations.note: Gilgamesh kills and decapitates Humbaba with Enkidu’s assistance.

relations.myth: Enkidu helps capture the forest guardian
relations.note: Enkidu accompanies Gilgamesh, confronts Humbaba, and urges immediate execution.

relations.myth: Gilgamesh and Enkidu behead the pleading guardian
relations.note: Enkidu participates in Humbaba’s killing and presses Gilgamesh not to spare him.
The epic calls Humbaba’s personified supernatural defenses his seven sons.
